1: //! # pathland-view
2: //!
3: //! The Pathland SwiftUI-style view DSL. Core components (`VStack`, `HStack`,
4: //! `Text`) and chainable modifiers (`spacing`, `padding`, `font_size`, `color`,
5: //! `background`) build a retained **view tree** (`Node`) that
6: //! `pathland-engine` turns into declarative `TREE`/`STYLE` opcodes.
7: //!
8: //! ## Building a tree
9: //!
10: //! Use the `vstack!`/`hstack!` macros (which box children for you) with the
11: //! free `text`/`spacer` functions, then chain modifiers and `build()`:
12: //!
13: //! ```
14: //! use pathland_view::{vstack, hstack, text, View, ViewExt};
15: //!
16: //! let node = vstack![
17: //!     text("a"),
18: //!     hstack![text("b")],
19: //! ]
20: //! .padding(16.0)
21: //! .build();
22: //! # let _ = node;
23: //! ```
24: //!
25: //! ## Decoupled modifiers
26: //!
27: //! Modifiers are **decoupled from views** (SwiftUI-style): any modifier applies
28: //! to any view via the blanket `View::modifier`, and application code composes
29: //! **custom modifiers** from the core ones by implementing `ViewModifier`:
30: //!
31: //! ```
32: //! use pathland_view::{View, ViewExt, ViewModifier, Node, Padding, Background};
33: //!
34: //! struct Card;
35: //! impl ViewModifier for Card {
36: //!     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node) {
37: //!         Padding(16.0).apply(node);
38: //!         Background(0xFF_EEEEEE).apply(node);
39: //!     }
40: //! }
41: //!
42: //! // Works on any view:
43: //! let a = pathland_view::text("A").modifier(Card);
44: //! let b = pathland_view::vstack![].modifier(Card);
45: //! # let _ = (a, b);
46: //! ```
47: //!
48: //! Unsupported combinations are **allowed and ignored**: the modifier emits its
49: //! property and the renderer ignores what it cannot apply.
50: //!
51: //! ## No layout math
52: //!
53: //! The DSL describes structure + constraint properties only. It never computes
54: //! bounds; native renderers lay out their own elements.
55: //!
56: //! This crate is `no_std` + `alloc`.
57: 
58: #![no_std]
59: #![forbid(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn)]
60:

80: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
81: // Core component macros + free functions
82: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
83: 
84: /// Build a vertical stack from a comma-separated list of views.
85: ///
86: /// Each child is boxed automatically, so children can mix `Text`, `HStack`,
87: /// modified views, or custom `View` implementations. Nested stacks work:
88: ///
89: /// ```
90: /// use pathland_view::{vstack, text, View};
91: /// let node = vstack![text("a"), text("b")].build();
92: /// # let _ = node;
93: /// ```
94: #[macro_export]
95: macro_rules! vstack {
96:     ($($child:expr),* $(,)?) => {
97:         $crate::VStack::new().children($crate::vec![$($crate::Box::new($child)),*])
98:     };
99: }
100: 
101: /// Build a horizontal stack from a comma-separated list of views.
102: ///
103: /// See [`vstack!`] for details.
104: #[macro_export]
105: macro_rules! hstack {
106:     ($($child:expr),* $(,)?) => {
107:         $crate::HStack::new().children($crate::vec![$($crate::Box::new($child)),*])
108:     };
109: }

111: /// A text view from a string literal (shorthand for [`Text::new`]).
112: pub fn text(content: &str) -> Text {
113:     Text::new(content)

125: /// A node in the retained view tree (the application's canonical UI tree).
126: #[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
127: pub struct Node {
128:     /// Stable node id (0 until `assign_ids`).
129:     pub id: u32,
130:     pub component: Component,
131:     pub children: Vec<Node>,
132:     /// Fixed width or `None` (native renderer sizes naturally).
133:     pub width: Option<f32>,
134:     /// Fixed height or `None` (native renderer sizes naturally).
135:     pub height: Option<f32>,
136:     /// Constraint/style properties (propertyId → value) emitted as
137:     /// `STYLE:SET_PROPERTY`.
138:     pub properties: BTreeMap<u16, u32>,
139: }

142:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
143:         f.debug_struct("Node")
144:             .field("id", &self.id)
145:             .field("component", &self.component)
146:             .field("children", &self.children)
147:             .field("width", &self.width)

150:             .finish()
151:     }

168: /// Core component types. These describe **structure only** — spacing, padding,
169: /// and sizing arrive as modifiers (properties), never as layout math here.
170: #[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
171: pub enum Component {
172:     /// Vertical stack (native vertical container).
173:     VStack,
174:     /// Horizontal stack (native horizontal container).
175:     HStack,
176:     /// Text leaf.
177:     Text { text: String },
178:     /// Interactive button.
179:     Button { label: String },
180:     /// Flexible spacer.
181:     Spacer,
182: }

184: impl core::fmt::Debug for Component {
185:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
186:         match self {
187:             Component::VStack => f.write_str("VStack"),
188:             Component::HStack => f.write_str("HStack"),
189:             Component::Text { text } => f.debug_tuple("Text").field(text).finish(),
190:             Component::Button { label } => f.debug_tuple("Button").field(label).finish(),
191:             Component::Spacer => f.write_str("Spacer"),
192:         }
193:     }
194: }

196: /// Map a component to its protocol component type id.
197: pub fn component_type_id(component: &Component) -> u16 {
198:     match component {
199:         Component::VStack => component_type::VSTACK,
200:         Component::HStack => component_type::HSTACK,
201:         Component::Text { .. } => component_type::TEXT,
202:         Component::Button { .. } => component_type::BUTTON,
203:         Component::Spacer => component_type::SPACER,
204:     }
205: }

207: /// The protocol value type for a property id.
208: ///
209: /// Color-valued properties (COLOR, BACKGROUND_COLOR, …) are emitted with the
210: /// `COLOR` value type; all other constraint/style properties are `F32`.
211: pub fn value_type_for(prop: u16) -> u8 {
212:     match prop {
213:         property_id::COLOR
214:         | property_id::BACKGROUND_COLOR
215:         | property_id::BORDER_COLOR => pathland_opcode::value_type::COLOR,
216:         _ => pathland_opcode::value_type::F32,
217:     }
218: }

220: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
221: // View protocol
222: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
223: 
224: /// A composable view. Implement for custom views; the core components and
225: /// `Modified` wrappers implement it already.
226: pub trait View {
227:     /// Build the retained node for this view.
228:     fn build(&self) -> Node;
229: }
230: 
231: /// A view decorator (SwiftUI `ViewModifier`): transforms a node's properties.
232: ///
233: /// Core modifiers (`Spacing`, `Padding`, `FontSize`, `Color`, `Background`)
234: /// implement this; application code implements it to compose custom modifiers.
235: pub trait ViewModifier {
236:     /// Apply the modifier to `node` (mutating constraint properties).
237:     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node);
238: }
239: 
240: /// A view wrapped by a modifier (SwiftUI `some View` nesting).
241: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
242: pub struct Modified<V, M> {
243:     view: V,
244:     modifier: M,
245: }
246: 
247: impl<V: View, M: ViewModifier> View for Modified<V, M> {
248:     fn build(&self) -> Node {
249:         let mut node = self.view.build();
250:         self.modifier.apply(&mut node);
251:         node
252:     }
253: }
254: 
255: /// Blanket modifier methods on any `View`.
256: ///
257: /// `.modifier(...)` applies a custom (or core) modifier; the sugar methods
258: /// (`spacing`, `padding`, `font_size`, `color`, `background`) are conveniences
259: /// that construct the corresponding core modifier. Modifiers apply
260: /// innermost-first, matching SwiftUI ordering.
261: pub trait ViewExt: View + Sized {
262:     /// Apply a modifier to this view.
263:     fn modifier<M: ViewModifier>(self, modifier: M) -> Modified<Self, M> {
264:         Modified { view: self, modifier }
265:     }
266: 
267:     /// Chain `.spacing(value)`.
268:     fn spacing(self, value: f32) -> Modified<Self, Spacing> {
269:         self.modifier(Spacing(value))
270:     }
271: 
272:     /// Chain `.padding(value)`.
273:     fn padding(self, value: f32) -> Modified<Self, Padding> {
274:         self.modifier(Padding(value))
275:     }
276: 
277:     /// Chain `.font_size(value)`.
278:     fn font_size(self, value: f32) -> Modified<Self, FontSize> {
279:         self.modifier(FontSize(value))
280:     }
281: 
282:     /// Chain `.color(rgba)` (sRGB `0xAARRGGBB`).
283:     fn color(self, rgba: u32) -> Modified<Self, Color> {
284:         self.modifier(Color(rgba))
285:     }
286: 
287:     /// Chain `.background(rgba)` (sRGB `0xAARRGGBB`).
288:     fn background(self, rgba: u32) -> Modified<Self, Background> {
289:         self.modifier(Background(rgba))
290:     }
291: }
292: 
293: impl<T: View> ViewExt for T {}

I have all the information needed. Both crates are single-file `lib.rs` modules, and I've cross-checked the opcode constants, the `Guest` API, the guest component state, and the WIT world to confirm what exists and what does not.

# Architecture Investigation Report

## 1. `pathland-view` — `crates/pathland-view/src/lib.rs`

### `Node` struct (lines 126–166)

```rust
pub struct Node {                          // line 127
    pub id: u32,                           // line 129  — stable node id (0 until assign_ids)
    pub component: Component,              // line 130
    pub children: Vec<Node>,               // line 131  — owned recursive children
    pub width: Option<f32>,                // line 133  — fixed width, None = native size
    pub height: Option<f32>,               // line 135  — fixed height, None = native size
    pub properties: BTreeMap<u16, u32>,    // line 138  — propertyId → value (STYLE:SET_PROPERTY)
}
```

- Derives `Clone, PartialEq` (line 126); manual `Debug` at lines 141–152.
- **Retained-tree representation**: a plain owned recursive `Vec<Node>`. There is no arena, no parent pointers, no weak handles — it is a value tree.
- `Node::from_component(component)` (lines 154–166) builds an empty node (id 0, no children, no properties).

### `Component` enum (lines 170–182)

Exactly five variants, all structural (no layout math):

```rust
pub enum Component {                       // line 171
    VStack,                                // line 173
    HStack,                                // line 175
    Text { text: String },                 // line 177
    Button { label: String },              // line 179
    Spacer,                                // line 181
}
```

Derives `Clone, PartialEq`; manual `Debug` at 184–194. Note: `Component` only covers 5 of the 12 protocol component types (the protocol also defines IMAGE, SWITCH, TEXT_FIELD, SCROLLVIEW, LIST, GRID, COMMENT — see `constants.rs` lines 104–111, none of which have DSL wrappers here).

- `component_type_id(&Component) -> u16` (lines 197–205) maps variants to protocol IDs: VStack→`VSTACK`(0x0002), HStack→`HSTACK`(0x0001), Text→`TEXT`(0x0003), Button→`BUTTON`(0x0004), Spacer→`SPACER`(0x0008).
- `value_type_for(prop) -> u8` (lines 211–218): COLOR/BACKGROUND_COLOR/BORDER_COLOR → `value_type::COLOR`(0x07), everything else → `F32`.

### Traits

```rust
pub trait View {                           // line 226
    fn build(&self) -> Node;               // line 228
}

pub trait ViewModifier {                   // line 235
    fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node);      // line 237
}
```

### `Modified<V, M>` wrapper (lines 241–253)

```rust
pub struct Modified<V, M> {                // line 242
    view: V,
    modifier: M,
}

impl<V: View, M: ViewModifier> View for Modified<V, M> {   // line 247
    fn build(&self) -> Node {
        let mut node = self.view.build();  // line 249 — inner view first
        self.modifier.apply(&mut node);    // line 250 — then modifier mutates it
        node
    }
}
```

**Critical semantics**: modifiers do **not** create wrapper tree nodes. `Modified::build` builds the inner node and then mutates the *same* node's `properties` BTreeMap in place. Tree depth in `Node` corresponds only to VStack/HStack nesting — modifier chains are flattened into the property map. Ordering is innermost-first (test at lines 655–663 proves `padding(4).padding(8)` → 8 wins).

### `ViewExt` sugar (lines 261–293)

Blanket trait on `View + Sized`; blanket impl for all `T: View` at line 293. Methods:
- `modifier<M: ViewModifier>(self, m: M) -> Modified<Self, M>` (line 263)
- `spacing(f32)` (line 268) → `Spacing`
- `padding(f32)` (line 273) → `Padding`
- `font_size(f32)` (line 278) → `FontSize`
- `color(u32)` (line 283) → `Color`
- `background(u32)` (line 288) → `Background`

There is **no** `.width()`/`.height()` sugar — those `Node` fields exist but can only be set by direct Node construction (they are never set via the DSL path or the WIT builder).

### Core modifiers (lines 300–348)

All are tuple structs implementing `ViewModifier::apply` by inserting into `node.properties`:
- `Spacing(pub f32)` → `property_id::SPACING` (0x0001), stored as `f32::to_bits()` (lines 319–323)
- `Padding(pub f32)` → `PADDING` (0x0004), `to_bits()` (325–329)
- `FontSize(pub f32)` → `FONT_SIZE` (0x1007), `to_bits()` (331–336)
- `Color(pub u32)` → `COLOR` (0x100A), raw `0xAARRGGBB` (338–342)
- `Background(pub u32)` → `BACKGROUND_COLOR` (0x1001), raw (344–348)

### Core components and `build()` collapse

- `VStack` (lines 355–395): field `children: Vec<Box<dyn View>>` (line 356); `View::build` (384–395) produces `Node { id: 0, component: Component::VStack, children: self.children.iter().map(|c| c.build()).collect(), ... }` — each child `Box<dyn View>` is collapsed to a `Node` recursively. **This is where `Box<dyn View>` (compile-time view graph) becomes `Vec<Node>` (retained value tree).**
- `HStack` (398–438): identical pattern.
- `Text` (441–466): `text: String`; `build` → `Component::Text { text: clone }`.
- `Spacer` (469–496): unit struct; `build` → `Component::Spacer`.
- `Button` (499–524): `label: String`; `build` → `Component::Button { label: clone }`.
- Free functions: `text(&str)` (112–114), `spacer()` (117–119), `button(&str)` (527–529).

### `vstack!`/`hstack!` macros (lines 94–109)

```rust
macro_rules! vstack {                      // line 95
    ($($child:expr),* $(,)?) => {
        $crate::VStack::new().children($crate::vec![$($crate::Box::new($child)),*])
    };
}
```

`hstack!` is identical (lines 104–109). They box children automatically so children can be heterogeneous (`Text`, `HStack`, `Modified`, custom `View`s). `Box` and `vec!` are re-exported at crate root for hygiene (lines 71, 73).

### `assign_ids` (lines 539–545)

```rust
pub fn assign_ids(root: &mut Node, next: &mut u32) {   // line 539
    root.id = *next;
    *next += 1;
    for child in &mut root.children {
        assign_ids(child, next);                        // line 543
    }
}
```

Pre-order, root first, sequential (test at 666–673: root=1, children=2,3, grandchild=4). The doc comment (lines 536–538) states the contract: **the engine keys its diff snapshot by node id, so call this after building the (possibly re-built) tree and before `Engine::emit`.** Stable ids across rebuilds are the entire basis for diffing.

---

## 2. `pathland-engine` — `crates/pathland-engine/src/lib.rs`

### `SnapshotNode` (lines 60–71)

```rust
struct SnapshotNode {                      // line 61
    component_type: u16,                   // line 62
    parent: Option<u32>,                   // line 63
    index: usize,                          // line 64
    text: Option<String>,                  // line 65
    width: Option<f32>,                    // line 66
    height: Option<f32>,                   // line 67
    properties: BTreeMap<u16, u32>,        // line 68
    gen: u64,                              // line 69  — generation stamp for deletion detection
}
```

This is the **only** state the engine remembers — it is a snapshot of the *last emitted* tree, not the application state.

### `Engine` struct (lines 89–94)

```rust
pub struct Engine {                        // line 89
    snapshot: Vec<Option<SnapshotNode>>,   // line 91  — nodeId → last emitted state (preallocated slab)
    gen: u64,                              // line 93  — monotonic generation stamp for current pass
}
```

`new()` at 103–108; `Default` at 96–100. `tracked_nodes()` diagnostic at 135–137. `slot_mut(id)` (139–145) resizes the slab on demand (allocation only when the tree *grows*).

### `emit()` — diff-based reactive emission (lines 111–132)

```rust
pub fn emit(&mut self, root: &Node, guest: &mut Guest<'_>)
    -> Result<EmitResult, pathland_opcode::RingError> {   // line 111
    self.gen = self.gen.wrapping_add(1);                  // line 116
    let mut out = 0usize;
    self.reconcile_node(root, None, 0, guest, &mut out)?; // line 118
    // Delete sweep: any snapshot slot not visited this pass has stale gen.   // 121–130
    for (id, slot) in self.snapshot.iter_mut().enumerate() {
        if let Some(s) = slot {
            if s.gen != self.gen {
                guest.delete_node(id as u32)?;            // line 125  DELETE_NODE
                *out += 1;
                *slot = None;                             // line 127
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(EmitResult { opcodes: out })                       // line 131
}
```

Algorithm: bump generation → reconcile the passed tree recursively → sweep the snapshot slab for any entry whose generation stamp was not refreshed (i.e., not visited this pass) and emit `DELETE_NODE`. `EmitResult` (lines 78–82) just counts opcodes.

### `reconcile_node` (lines 147–296)

Signature (lines 148–155): `(&mut self, node: &Node, parent: Option<u32>, index: usize, guest: &mut Guest<'_>, out: &mut usize)`.

Preliminaries:
- `component_type = component_type_id(&node.component)` (line 156).
- `text_borrowed`: text of `Text` or label of `Button`, else `None` (lines 158–162).
- `let prev = self.slot_mut(node.id).take()` (line 164) — **pops the previous snapshot entry; `prev == None` means "new node", `prev == Some(p)` means "existing node"**. This is the entire new-vs-existing detection mechanism.
- `props_changed` (165–168) and `text_changed` (170–173) computed without cloning.

**New-node arm (`None`, lines 177–193)** emits, in order:
1. `guest.create_node(node.id, component_type)` → `TREE:CREATE_NODE` (line 178)
2. `guest.insert_child(p, node.id, index)` → `TREE:INSERT_CHILD` (only if parent exists, line 181)
3. Every property: `guest.set_property(node.id, prop, value_type_for(prop), value)` → `STYLE:SET_PROPERTY` (lines 184–187)
4. `emit_size_props` → WIDTH/HEIGHT properties (line 188; helper at 299–324)
5. `guest.set_text(node.id, t)` → `STYLE:SET_TEXT` for Text/Button (lines 189–192)

**Existing-node arm (`Some(p)`, lines 194–255)**, diffed against the snapshot:
1. **Parent moved** (`p.parent != parent`, lines 196–204): emits `REMOVE_CHILD(old, node.id)` if there was an old parent, then `INSERT_CHILD(new, node.id, index)` if there is a new one.
2. **Reordered** (`p.index != index` within same parent, lines 205–210): emits `MOVE_CHILD(par, node.id, index)` → `TREE:MOVE_CHILD`.
3. **Component type changed** (lines 212–215): re-emits `CREATE_NODE` (protocol has no "change type" opcode — the host recreates the element).
4. **Text changed** (lines 217–222): `SET_TEXT`.
5. **Width/height diffs** (lines 224–245): `SET_PROPERTY` with WIDTH/HEIGHT. Note: only the `Some` → `Some` change direction emits; clearing a size (Some → None) emits nothing.
6. **Property map diff** (lines 246–254): iterates `node.properties` and emits `SET_PROPERTY` only for keys where `p.properties.get(prop) != Some(value)`. **Removed properties emit no opcode** (no "unset property" exists in the protocol).

After the match, the new snapshot entry is stored (lines 261–290):
- Zero-alloc optimization: if `props_changed`/`text_changed` were false, the previous `BTreeMap`/`String` allocations are **moved back** into the new `SnapshotNode` (lines 264–271); only changed fields are freshly allocated (273–280). This is what makes steady-state emission allocation-free.
- Snapshot written with `gen: self.gen` (lines 281–290).
- Recursion into children: `reconcile_node(child, Some(node.id), i, ...)` (lines 292–294).

### Does the engine hold a retained tree?

**No.** `Engine` holds only the diff snapshot (`snapshot` slab + `gen`). The caller passes a fresh `&Node` to `emit` on every frame (line 112). The retained tree lives elsewhere:

- In the **native Rust** path: in the application (e.g., a struct holding a `Node` the app mutates and re-passes).
- In the **WASM guest** path (`crates/pathland-guest/src/lib.rs`): the retained tree is a flat id-indexed map `State.nodes: HashMap<u32, FlatNode>` (lines 42–48, 56). Every `emit()` call **re-materializes the entire `Node` tree from scratch** via `materialize(&s.nodes, root_id)` (lines 109–120, called at line 214), then passes it to `engine.emit(&root, &mut ring)`. So the full tree is re-authored from the flat builder state on every emit — the DSL `build()` in the pure-Rust path similarly rebuilds a fresh `Node` from the view structs each time.

### Dependency tracking: **Does not exist**

I searched all crates for `signal|dirty|depend|invalidate|memo|reactive|subscribe`. Findings:

- The **only** hits in `pathland-engine` are doc comments:
  - Lines 15–16: *"This is what signals in the application drive — a signal marks the tree dirty; `emit` reconciles."*
  - Line 84: `/// The diff-based reactive emitter.`
  - These are **aspirational documentation only** — there is no signal type, no `dirty` flag, no dependency graph, no memoization, no invalidation mechanism, no subscription primitive anywhere in the crate (or in `pathland-view`, `pathland-guest`, or the WIT world `wit/pathland.wit`).
- The guest's `builder` interface (`create-node`, `insert-child`, `remove-child`, `set-text`, `set-property`) mutates the flat map with **no change tracking** — `create_node` even unconditionally clears all properties (guest lib.rs lines 135–144).
- `AGENTS.md` confirms this is a known gap: *"Planned / deferred: signals (Goal 2/#13)"*.

**Conclusion**: Reconciliation is **pure tree-to-snapshot structural diffing** of two full trees. There is no link from application state to view nodes. The application (or WIT host) is responsible for (a) detecting that something changed, (b) mutating the retained tree (Node properties / flat map), (c) re-authoring/re-passing the full `&Node`, and (d) calling `emit`. The engine only diff-compares the freshly passed tree against what it last emitted, keyed by stable node ids assigned via `assign_ids` / host-supplied ids. An unchanged tree emits exactly zero opcodes (test, lines 502–512), and steady-state emission provably performs zero heap allocations (test, lines 515–563).

### Opcode coverage summary

The engine emits exactly these protocol commands (constants in `pathland-opcode/src/constants.rs`):
- `TREE:CREATE_NODE` (0x01, line 23), `TREE:DELETE_NODE` (0x02, line 25), `TREE:INSERT_CHILD` (0x03, line 27), `TREE:REMOVE_CHILD` (0x04, line 29), `TREE:MOVE_CHILD` (0x05, line 31)
- `STYLE:SET_PROPERTY` (0x01, line 37), `STYLE:SET_TEXT` (0x03, line 41)
- All funneled through the `Guest` API in `pathland-opcode/src/lib.rs` (lines 151–201).
